text: As expected, China threw a fit. Not content with their punitive 84% tariff, they dragged the U.S. before the World Trade Organization—an intergovernmental organization (IGO) formed by treaties between countries and composed of member states—and slapped 11 American companies, including military suppliers like American Photonics and SYNEXXUS, onto their so-called “unreliable entities” list. The hypocrisy is staggering. This is the same China that bullies smaller nations like Vietnam and the Philippines over contested territory in the South China Sea, blatantly ignoring a binding ruling from the United Nations, another intergovernmental organization. Outside the White House, Treasury Secretary nominee Scott Bessent couldn’t hide his admiration. “We saw the successful negotiating strategy that President Trump implemented a week ago today. It has brought more than 75 countries forward to negotiate,” Bessent told the reporters. “It took great courage for him to stay the course until this moment. And what we have ended up with here, as I told everyone a week ago, in this very spot, do not retaliate and you will be rewarded. So every country in the world who wants to come and negotiate, we are willing to hear you. We’re going to go down to a 10% baseline tariff for them, and China will be raised to 125 due to their insistence on escalation.” — Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) April 9, 2025 The markets exploded on the news, with the Dow surging 2,963 points (7.87%), the S&P 500 rocketing 9.52% (third-largest one-day gain since World War II), and the Nasdaq soaring 12.16% (largest one-day rise since January 2001 and the second-best performance in its history). This comes after Trump paused the tariffs and advised everyone to buy the dip, stating , “THIS IS A GREAT TIME TO BUY!!! DJT.” For reference, this was the largest point moves EVER to the upside in the DOW, Nasdaq, and S&P 500 $SPY . Insane. pic.twitter.com/nuFAILw9vc — unusual_whales (@unusual_whales) April 9, 2025
